(1) the implementation of bilingual policy in Paraguay produced differential outcomes for students, (2) these outcomes were produced in part through the scalar effects of the policy, and (3) a scalar frame of analysis is useful for understanding the differential outcomes of policy and for suggesting ways to make policy more effective for minoritized students.

the scalar analysis of the implementation of Paraguayan language-in-education policy shows that the implementation of policy is a process of negotiation between the policy itself and the local conditions in which the policy is implemented.
The main takeaway from our work is that
policy analysis needs to take account of multiple scales of time and place, and that the scalar frame is a useful way to do this.
the scalar approach to policy analysis is a useful way to think about the relationship between language policy, language use, and social inequality.

the scalar frame can help researchers and policymakers to identify the multiple and heterogeneous scales involved in the implementation of educational language policies and, in so doing, to better understand how to make policy work to the benefit of all children.
